title: Multi-Lane Response Profiles PRD and Staged Launch Playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Objective: Deliver a PRD and operational playbook for 'Multi‑Lane Response Profiles' — a unified behavioral and perf configuration that lets customers choose response modes (Latency‑First, Cost‑Optimized, Quality‑Guarded) across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints. Background: customers require predictable economics and consistent behavior when migrating between hosted, dedicated, and private lanes. Problem statement: current endpoint surface exposes per-endpoint knobs but lacks a unified, discoverable profile model and rollout/checklist for production readiness. Scope: deliver API schema additions (profile param), console UX for selecting profiles, server-side mapping to batching/quantization/routing policies, default profile set, telemetry and SLO targets, and a staged launch playbook. Out of scope: model training changes, new quantization algorithms, private on‑prem installer changes beyond config flags. Key decisions to make: canonical profile names and semantics, priority of routing fallbacks, default profile for free-tier vs paid customers, minimum telemetry retention for profile validation. Stakeholders: PM (Aisha), Eng leads (Serving Runtime: Marta Reyes, Console: Chen Li), Design (R&D UX: Priya Menon), Security/Compliance (Oliver Park). Success metrics: adoption rate of profiles within 6 weeks, end‑to‑end latency and cost delta per profile, regression free signal rate <=1% on critical evals. This PRD includes acceptance criteria and a stepwise launch checklist that embeds canary metrics, rollback gates, and post-launch monitoring tasks.
acceptance_criteria: API: profile param accepted on chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints with backwards-compatible default behavior
Console: profile selector appears in endpoint creation and route settings with inline help text and guardrails
Runtime: each profile maps to documented batching, KV caching, and kernel selection policies; routing respects profile prioritization
Telemetry: per-profile token-level cost, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and quality regressions reported in Console dashboards
E2E tests: automated smoke tests validating output format and stability for each profile across representative models
Contracts: behavior-preserving defaults for existing customers; breaking changes require explicit migration path
Security: profile metadata is logged and audited; any changes to profile selection are captured by RBAC audit trails
Performance: Latency‑First profile p95 on small prompt workload <= 250ms (hosted region standard GPU), Cost‑Optimized shows >= 12% cost reduction for batchy workloads without >10% quality regression
Rollout safety: canary with 5% traffic for 48 hours with no SLO breach before incremental ramp
launch_checklist: Finalize canonical profile definitions and include in API spec (PR to openapi repo)
Console UX shipped behind feature flag and validated with 3 internal teams
Runtime mappings implemented and feature-flagged; unit and integration tests green
Telemetry dashboards created: per-profile latency/cost/quality panels; alert rules configured
Canary plan documented with traffic slices, monitoring owners, and rollback criteria
Documentation: API examples, migration guide, cost/latency tradeoff doc, and FAQ published to docs site
Evals: run profile-specific evals on representative prompt sets for supported models; verify no quality regressions above threshold
Security review completed and signoff recorded (security checklist items closed)
Customer communications: draft beta announcement and support playbook for early adopters
SRE runbook: incident response steps and metric thresholds added to oncall handbook
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 48h observation windows; gating by p95 latency and error budget
Rollback plan: immediate revert to default profile routing plus quickfix knobs for per-customer overrides
Post-launch retrospective slot reserved and feedback loop for profile tuning enabled
